cities.d: the capital and largest city of the country.

x.around: You cannot return the card nor get a refund, think twice before adding too much money. However, you can use the card for several people, you just have to swipe for the second person as well. So, you might decide to only get one instead of two if you are traveling together. The free transfer between metro and bus for the other person does probably not work then.

hidden.d: The oldest church in the city. In the plaza, in front of the church, there is a Moaï from Easter Island.
Historical performance venue, including international dance and opera, worth a visit even if just from its outside.
One of the city's newest museums showcasing the human rights violations during the Pinochet dictatorship. It has English explanations to some of the showcasing.

n.en: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos

hidden.d: One of the city's major landmarks, next to Plaza de Armas.
The national museum showcases both the history and prehistory of today's Chile. There are several temporary themed exhibitions.
19th century palace owned by a wealthy Spanish-Portuguese family. The architecture is a mix of Spanish and French styles with inspiration taken from the Versailles palace.
Designed to resemble a traditional Chilean town, its narrow dirt streets and adobe houses with thatched roofs host workshops where artisans create and sell their crafts directly to visitors.

A colorful market with over 500 stalls, selling fruits, vegetables and other food products. The current market building was inaugurated a century ago but farmers have been selling their products at this place since colonial…

x.intro: Santiago is the capital and economic center of Chile. With its many museums, events, theaters, restaurants, bars and other entertainment and cultural opportunities, it is also the cultural center of the country. For visitors it's both the gateway to the country and a destination in its own right with an eclectic architecture, a vibrant culinary and cultural scene, surrounded by the mighty Andes welcoming skiers, trekkers and friends of wine.

must.d: This is the site of sports events (both football and others), concerts, and social events including the yearly Teletón charity event. A National Historical Landmark opened in 1938, the World Cup finals were played here in 1962.
South America's highest building with a viewing platform on the top floor.

The national library was built in the early 20th century near Cerro Santa Lucía. Here you can find archives of all Chilean newspapers and some foreign ones, map and photo archives and an exhibition hall.
Built to celebrate Chile's 100 year anniversary, this museum boasts 3000 art works from Chile and the rest of Latin America.
The well put-together Chilean Museum of Pre-Columbian Art houses various artefacts from Mesoamerica and South America, featuring cultures such as the Olmec, Maya, and Inca civilizations.
A park with fountains and stairs leading up to a fort and viewpoint the top. The summit has a great view of all but the skyscraper-obscured city center.

The lively little square in the intersection of the two most important avenues of Santiago, Alameda and Vicuña Mackenna is also frequently the place for public meetings such as celebrating sport successes and political…
Santiago's modern art museum is part of the university's faculty of art. Next to the façade there's a statue by the Colombian artist Fernando Botero.

n.es: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago

next.d: Valle Nevado, La Parva and El Colorado. The ski resorts of Portillo and Valle Nevado are two to three hours away on the road to Mendoza.
is 85 km to the south and has some thermal springs and hiking opportunities nearby.
90 minutes away is the beach capital of the country, and it also has nice parks, gardens, restaurants, cafes and casinos.
next to Vina del Mar is one of the largest ports on the Pacific, but certainly not a dirty industrial behemoth.

x.safe: Santiago is infamous for its smog, which is worse during the winter (May–September). The locals welcome the rain which falls during winters as it cleans the air. Be sure to carry bottled water with you during the summer. Be prepared for sauna-heat on the metro during summer.

cities.d: Chile's second largest city is a city rich in culture, history and beauty.

x.around: The Gran Concepción is the name that receives the whole metropolitan area, which includes Talcahuano, Hualpen, San Pedro de la Paz, Chiguayante, Hualqui and Penco.

hidden.d: A nice hike uphill on well maintained trails, through a eucalyptus forest. At the highest point of the Cerro Caracol there is a stone tower built in 1921 by the German community in Concepcíon as a tribute to the first chancellor…

x.intro: Concepción is Chile's second largest city with a population of almost 227,000 (out of Concepción province's 946,000) as of 2016. It is a city rich in culture, history and beauty on the coast of Southern Chile. The commune is home to historical bridges, murals, parks and lagoons, and to important cultural centers such as the Biobío Theater, the House of Art, the Natural History Museum and the University of Concepción Theater.

next.d: A ski town 2 hr from Concepción. Home to a large volcano with great skiing so visit in the winter or enjoy the thermal spas heated by the volcanic waters year-round.
An island that can be reached from Tirua, a journey 5 hr south by bus.
The capital is a 6-hour bus journey away and buses run frequently so if you need a taste of the big city life, it's not too far.

x.safe: The city is generally safe, however: * Be aware of pickpockets and avoid wearing expensive-looking jewelry or watches, even during the day. * Do not visit Talcahuano's seaport, Hualpen and near areas in the night, especially on weekends.

x.around: Micros run along the major streets in the center and takes you from the center to the Zofri in no time. Walking is the most convenient mode of transport for getting to and from the beaches.
x.intro: Iquique is a city of 191,000 people (2017) in the Northern Chile. The city is home to the Zofri duty-free zone, and a growing number of high-rise resort hotels along its beaches. Slightly more expensive and polluted than neighboring population centers, such as Arica, but a convenient place to stock up on duty-free perfumes and laptop computers.

must.d: This UNESCO site is an old residential and production site from the days of the saltpetre era. Few residential houses are furnished, but most of the site is still in remarkable condition due to the dry atmosphere.

n.es: Oficinas salitreras de Humberstone y Santa Laura
n.fr: usines de salpêtre de Humberstone et de Santa Laura
n.it: Raffinerie di salnitro di Humberstone e Santa Laura

must.d: The largest geoglyph in the region. A remarkable planning effort considering that it is hundreds of years old. You get the best overall picture when looking on Google Earth though; therefore you could stop there if you are…

next.d: Next main city north
North, gateway into Bolivia

cities.d: a charming city, with beautiful, well-preserved neocolonial architecture, and extensive beaches.

hidden.d: This museum has a record of more than 3,500 pieces, organized in history and fine arts, as well as various objects that illustrate the life of the president.

n.es: Museo Histórico de la Serena Gabriel González Videla

hidden.d: Neoclassical style house built in 1872. It still preserves various accessories such as stained glass windows and altars.

n.es: Capilla, casa y claustro de la Divina Providencia (La Serena)

hidden.d: This church was founded in 1558, but after several attacks it was finally rebuilt in 1830. The tower is in the Gothic style, and is considered the city's architectural heritage.

This museum has a record of more than 12,000 objects, distributed in three categories, archeology, where it characterizes regional pre-Hispanic cultures of Chile, ethnography, where objects from ethnic groups in the area are…
Eclectic-style church founded in 1672 by the Jesuits. Throughout history this church has suffered from various thefts and fires.

x.intro: La Serena is a charming city of about 200,000 people (2012) in Northern Chile. Its historic center stands out with a beautiful and well-preserved neocolonial architecture characterized by its balconies, small squares and stone churches of several centuries old, its extensive beaches and for being one of the cities with the best quality of life in Chile.

must.d: This cathedral is the first in the city, founded in 1544. On one side of this is the Plaza Juan Pablo II. Its stained glass windows were brought from France and its bell tower dates from the 20th century.

n.en: Cathedral of San Bartolomé de La Serena

must.d: The Japanese style (indeed, laid out by a Tokyo landscape architect) garden, celebrates the 450th anniversary of La Serena, its ties with its Japanese friend Tenri and the export of Chilean ore to Japan.

next.d: A few hours to the south.

cities.d: one of the southernmost cities of the world, it is an important starting point for trips to Antarctica and the Falkland Islands.

x.around: The city is built around its main square "Plaza de Armas" where the imposing monument of Hernando de Magallanes is located. There is also a monument of a Magellan native, or Ona, that according to local legend if a tourist touches his foot it will return once again to the city. Another local legend to come back to the city is to eat Magellan Barberries (calafate), similar to blueberries.

hidden.d: Monument to the leader of the first European expedition to this part of the world, standing in the middle of Plaza de Armas.
Here you can learn about the city's history and the sailors and explorers passing through.

The shepherd monument is a bronze sculpture showcasing a typical traditional profession on the Magellanican pampa. Considered a symbol of the city, there isn't much to do here than to take a couple of pictures.

Famous for its magnificent mausoleums, architecture, and shaped pine trees, the municipal cemetery dates back to the 1840s and is blessed with the remains of many local aristocratic families, as well as English and Croatian…
Regional museum, with historical artifacts and part of the Braun-Menéndez Mansion.
Next to Plaza de Armas.
A Salesian Society museum of natural history and pre-Colombian ethnic groups.
One of the main green areas of the city with picnic facilities, and a lake with canoes and kayaks in the summer, and a skating rink during the winter (when frozen over).

x.intro: Punta Arenas is the regional capital of the Magallanes y Antártica Region, in Chilean Patagonia, one of the southernmost cities in the world. It's the largest city in Chilean Patagonia, and has developed into a tourist center in far southern America rivaling Ushuaia in Argentina. It's an important starting point for trips to Antarctica and the Falkland Islands.

must.d: A nautically-themed museum that hosts replicas of the Nao Victoria, James Caird, Schooner Ancud and is building the first replica of the HMS Beagle.
The city's cathedral.

next.d: the southernmost point of mainland South America. Can be reached overland or by kayak. There are numerous companies in town that lead guided expeditions.
near Puerto Natales.

cities.d: visitors come in large numbers to use the town as a stepping stone to the amazing surrounding landscapes.

x.around: Outside of town you can even reach Valle de Marte on foot. Also, there are many hiking trails north and northwest of town. For reliable trails and GPS navigation in this desert region, consult OpenStreetMap, which is used by many mobile Apps like OsmAnd or Mapy.cz. Or just download the according GPX or KML files through Waymarked Trails for such trails on OpenStreetMap.

hidden.d: It features three different parts, all of them interesting

This is one amazing location in summer! Set in the northern tip of the Atacama salt pan, this location offers a splendid panorama of the Andes, and the possibility to bathe in waters as salty as those of the Dead Sea, meaning you…
Like most deserts, Atacama has its share of dunes and sand-banks. The most popular is located here. All sandboarding tours will take you there.

x.intro: San Pedro de Atacama is a town of 3,899 (2012) in Northern Chile. San Pedro is a very popular destination among Chilean tourists and international visitors looking for a desert experience and a stepping stone to the amazing landscapes around it. Most attractions are part of the Los Flamencos National Reserve, perhaps Chile's most varied and amazing national park.

must.d: 4200 above sea level, and some 100 away from town, these are one of the highest geysers in the world. It's also the third-largest geyser site on Earth, with over 80 active ones. Most agencies travel there at 04:00.
Commonly advertised as 'Moon Valley' in English, this part of the Salt Mountain Range offers stunning clinal and anticlinal formations in a perfectly barren landscape.

Feel like visiting the Atacama salt pan, a picturesque village, and some Alp-lookalikes in a single day? Plus eating some local food? Then consider this tour, usually advertised as 'Altiplanic Lagoons', the tour varies very…

It's perhaps San Pedro's best-kept secret. Or not. It really depends on your interests. The road is long, but well-paved, until you reach the entrance to the most remote part of the Los Flamencos national reservation: Monjes de…

They're commonly called 'Hot Springs', but that name couldn't be more of a misnomer. The Puritama (means 'hot water' in Kunza) is actually a warm river, that breaks loose from the stone a few meters away from the actual place.

next.d: As of April 2022, the timetable according to the sign at the bus terminal (incl. bus company) was the following
The most common way of traveling are three bus lines: Geminis, Andesmar, and Pullman Bus. The prices float around 30,000 pesos, and all of them leave from San Pedro three times per week.
Bolivia – Going this way can be done only from Calama; the fares are cheap, though, sometimes as low as 8,000 pesos.

x.safe: You can rest assured that there's virtually no violent crime in San Pedro. However, the theft of bicycles and cars happens every once in a while, so take the normal precautions in that regard. Despite being poorly lit at night, the town is safe to walk around at all times-use your common sense if you see something suspicious.

intro: Chile is a country in South America. Chile occupies a long, narrow strip of land between the Andes and the Pacific Ocean.

other.d: the largest island of the country.

hidden.d: Besides the trail along the coast from Rio Chepu to Chiloé National Park, this is another nice, easy-to-medium difficulty, and inexpensive (no boat required) trail between and which goes along the rough and picturesque coast at…

x.intro: Chiloé Island (Spanish: Isla de Chiloé) is in Southern Chile, off-shore from the northern Patagonian regions of Los Lagos and Aysén.

next.d: Not that touristy, more a busy working city, but gateway for trips to the nearby Alerce Andino National Park and Hornopirén further south.
Similar to Frutillar but larger.

x.safe: Southern Chile seafood (mussels, clams and other bivalve molluscs) could be infected with a poisonous alga which has potentially lethal effects. So always get your seafood from authorized sites.

x.around: It's easy to get around Pichilemu in taxi, colectivo taxi, walking, and on bike.

hidden.d: The wooden railway station.

x.intro: Pichilemu is a holiday town with beaches in Central Chile, south of Valparaíso. Pichilemu is a crossbreed of a sleepy fishing village and an international surf destination. Pichilemu is not quite on the Gringo Trail, but visitors from Chile and abroad quickly take to this rapidly growing town.

n.en: Agustín Ross Cultural Centre and Park

other.d: well known for its jungles and endemic flora

x.intro: Juan Fernández Islands is a small archipelago 670 km off the coast of Central Chile. They are remote islands, home to about 900 people who survive on lobster fishing and several hundred tourists who make the obscure islands a vacation destination each year. The rugged, mountainous islands are quite attractive, but you won't find white sand beaches, and the water is much colder than the weather might indicate, owing to the northerly Humboldt Current.

other.d: a wine and pisco producing area, also known for its astronomical observatories.

x.around: Renting a truck or 4WD in Antofagasta or Calama is a great idea if you are 3-5 people and want to explore the region around on your own. This will save you a lot of money on expensive tours in San Pedro de Atacama, and rental cars are much cheaper in Antofagasta or Calama. But due to the rough terrain, it is strongly recommended to get a 4WD or truck, instead of a regular, unless you plan to stay on proper roads.
x.intro: Northern Chile is among the driest parts of the world. It includes the regions of Arica-Parinacota, Tarapacá, Antofagasta, Atacama and Coquimbo.
x.safe: Be aware that you can easily get up to more than 4,000 of altitude on normal roads. Get accustomed to this by getting higher in reasonable steps. If you join one of those one-day excursions from Arica to Lauca National Park then you are very likely to suffer from altitude sickness which must be taken seriously.

other.d: breathtaking desert landscape with impressive sand dunes and rock formations.
